extracted.intended_audience: MathML implementers, authoring-tool developers, renderer/readers, and document maintainers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and prescriptive rules for implementing, validating, transforming, and authoring Content/Presentation MathML so as to be conformant with MathML 4.0 and to convert arbitrary content MathML to Strict Content MathML.

rubrics_metrics.name: MathML-input-conformant
rubrics_metrics.description: An application that accepts all valid MathML expressions (including those containing presentation markup) may be characterized as MathML-input-conformant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementations should accept valid MathML input; handling of deprecated features affects compatibility with older MathML versions (see deprecated-features entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: MathML-output-conformant
rubrics_metrics.description: An equation editor or authoring tool that exports valid MathML for expressions it can convert is MathML-output-conformant; it may display errors for expressions it cannot convert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors/translators may generate valid MathML for convertible expressions and signal conversion failure (or emit merror) for others. Developers are encouraged to verify output using available validators.

rubrics_metrics.name: MathML-round-trip-conformant
rubrics_metrics.description: A processor is MathML-round-trip-conformant if it preserves MathML equivalence on expressions containing no deprecated features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Round-trip conformance is defined only with respect to expressions that contain no deprecated features; processors need only preserve equivalence for those expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the MathML Test Suite
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the W3C MathML Test Suite to give a quantitative statement about which parts of MathML are meaningfully implemented by an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developers who do not implement parts of the specification are encouraged to itemize omitted parts by referring to specific categories in the test suite. Customers are encouraged to use the test suites to verify implementer claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: MathML Validator usage
rubrics_metrics.description: For MathML-output-conformant processors, information about available tools to validate MathML is maintained at the W3C MathML Validator and developers are encouraged to verify their output using this validator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run produced MathML through the W3C MathML Validator as part of validation and QA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on generating deprecated features (output-conformant)
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to be MathML-output-conformant, authoring tools may not generate MathML markup containing deprecated features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authoring tools must avoid emitting deprecated 1.x/2.x constructs when conforming as MathML 4.0 output providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for deprecated features for older-version input-conformance
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to be MathML-input-conformant with MathML 1.x or 2.x, rendering and reading tools must support deprecated features; they do not have to support deprecated features to be considered in conformance with MathML 4.0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers targeting compatibility with older MathML versions should implement deprecated forms; MathML 4.0 implementations may omit them but are encouraged to support old forms where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test-suite-based itemization of omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Developers who choose not to implement parts of the MathML specification are encouraged to itemize the parts they leave out by referring to specific categories in the test suite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide consumers with precise references to test-suite categories to communicate coverage/limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No conformance requirements for extension mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML makes no conformance requirements concerning the use of extension mechanisms (mglyph, maction attributes from other namespaces, definitionURL/cd/content dictionaries), even when alternative standard markup is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although extensions are permitted, authors and implementers are strongly encouraged to use standard markup whenever possible and to monitor standards (Unicode/OpenMath) to update documents as standard markup becomes available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of invalid input (input-conformant apps)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a MathML-input-conformant application receives input containing elements with illegal attributes or child schemata, it should attempt to render valid parts and render error messages (as if enclosed in an merror element) in place of invalid expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gracefully degrade: render valid subexpressions, and show explicit error markers for invalid parts rather than silently ignoring or producing misleading valid markup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signalling errors in output (output-conformant apps)
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML-output-conformant applications such as editors and translators may choose to generate merror expressions to signal errors in their input; this is usually preferable to generating valid but possibly erroneous MathML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer explicit merror markup to producing valid-looking but semantically incorrect output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes for unspecified data — deprecation of other attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: The MathML 1.0 'other' attribute (a hook for renderer-specific information) is deprecated in MathML 2.0 and removed in MathML 4.0; namespace prefixes or data-* attributes should be used instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From MathML 4.0 onwards, use data-* or namespace-qualified attributes for non-standard renderer-specific information. Use non-standard attributes judiciously and not as a loophole to circumvent core conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use non-standard attributes judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: The intent of allowing non-standard attributes is not to encourage developers to circumvent core conventions; authors and applications should use non-standard attributes judiciously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit non-standard attributes to genuine renderer-specific needs and prefer standardized markup whenever possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Web platform implementations of MathML should implement MathML-Core, and the Privacy Considerations specified there apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow privacy guidance in MathML-Core when implementing MathML in web platform contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security considerations and XML parsing
rubrics_metrics.description: Web platform implementations of MathML should implement MathML-Core, and the Security Considerations specified there apply; when MathML expressions can be parsed as XML, apply XML parsing security considerations per RFC7303.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of XML parsing vulnerabilities and follow the referenced security guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Content MathML operator syntax and classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Operator elements have specific syntax, allowed child elements, operator classes (argument expectations), and qualifiers; implementations must follow the syntax tables for Content MathML constructors, attributes, operators, and qualifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the operator tables (Name, Content, Symbol(s), Class, Qualifiers) to determine valid children, argument counts, and mapping rules to Strict Content MathML.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict Content MathML Transformation — algorithmic mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Content MathML semantics are underpinned by a defined mapping to Strict Content MathML; the mapping is defined algorithmically as a sequence of nine steps, each applied repeatedly until no further application is possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement the multi-pass rewrite algorithm (or an equivalent recursive implementation) to transform arbitrary content MathML into Strict Content MathML deterministically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewrite non-strict bind
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace the bind tag in each binding expression with apply if it has qualifiers or multiple non-bvar child elements; later rules will change introduced apply elements back to bind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This normalization permits subsequent rules to uniformly handle non-strict binding expressions. Ensure later steps restore strict bind form where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply special-case rules for idiomatic qualifiers (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special-case rewrite rules must be applied for idiomatic uses of qualifiers (e.g., derivatives, integrals, limits, sums/products) to make binding status and qualifier semantics explicit for strict markup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle operator-specific qualifier idioms before generic qualifier rewriting to domainofapplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewrite derivatives (diff) to make binding explicit
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewrite diff (and nthdiff, partialdiffdegree) constructs so that the binding status of variables is explicit in Strict Content MathML (e.g., translate a diff applied to an expression-in-x to an application of diff to a lambda so the differentiated function is applied to x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that in strict form the differentiated function is represented as a lambda applied to the free variable, exposing free vs bound variable status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewrite nthdiff when degree present
rubrics_metrics.description: If the bvar element contains a degree element, use the nthdiff symbol (csymbol calculus1:nthdiff) and translate according to the specified pattern (nthdiff with degree, then bind lambda over variable and apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the provided example translations: use nthdiff with the degree as first argument and bind the function as a lambda, then apply to the variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewrite partialdiffdegree for partial derivatives with degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: If partialdiff is used with an expression and bvar qualifiers, rewrite to Strict Content MathML using the partialdiffdegree symbol; use cn 1 for any bound variable lacking a degree; if total-degree not used, second argument is the sum of degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble a list argument of degrees and the total (sum) as required; bind the expression with lambda over the bvars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewrite integrals (int, defint, defint limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate int elements to calculus1:int (indefinite) with a lambda binding the integrand; definite integrals map to calculus1:defint, and definite integrals with lowlimit/uplimit pairs map to defint with an oriented_interval (oriented_interval used to capture orientation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When bound variables are present introduce lambda; for lowlimit/uplimit use oriented_interval(a,b) to capture orientation and assumed left-to-right integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewrite limits and tendsto qualifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: tendsto qualifiers used to qualify a limit should be rewritten to an annotated identifier (semantics/annotation-xml) and limit conditions rewritten into a limit csymbol with appropriate null symbol depending on the tendsto type attribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rewrite: tendsto and Rewrite: limits condition patterns so the limit expression is represented by the limit csymbol, the target value, and a lambda over the bound expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewrite sums and products with bound variables
rubrics_metrics.description: When sums or products use bound variables, introduce a lambda construct so the expression in bound variables becomes a function; sums/products with qualifiers are rewritten according to n-ary sum/product rules (e.g., use integer_interval for lowlimit/uplimit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: sum with bvar i lowlimit 0 uplimit 100 rewrites to arith1:sum applied to integer_interval(0,100) and a bind lambda over i of the summed expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewrite qualifiers to domainofapplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewrite all apply constructions using bvar and qualifiers to those using only the general domainofapplication qualifier; multiple condition qualifiers become a single conjunction and multiple domainofapplication qualifiers become their intersection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalize qualifiers early so subsequent rules can handle domain restrictions uniformly; convert idiomatic qualifiers (interval, lowlimit/uplimit, condition) into domainofapplication forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalize container markup (sets, lists, vectors, matrices, intervals, piecewise, lambda, piecewise pieces)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewrite sets, lists, intervals, vectors, matrices, matrixrows, lambda expressions and piecewise functions to their normalized forms; any qualifiers will have been rewritten to domainofapplication and will be rewritten further in later steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the specified Rewrite: n-ary setlist domainofapplication and other container normalization rules so containers are in canonical forms for strict transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply special-case rules for operators using domainofapplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle special-case rewrites for operators when a domainofapplication qualifier is present (e.g., rewrite min/max/mean n-ary/unary operators, rewrite quantifiers forall/exists into implication/conjunction, rewrite integrals/sums/products with domainofapplication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform operator-specific transformations to correctly reflect domain restrictions (e.g., quantifiers become logical combinations, sums over domain become sum over restricted domain constructs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate domainofapplication (rewrite to restricted constructs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewrite domainofapplication into one of: an application of a restricted function via Rewrite: restriction (if no bvar), an application of predicate_on_list for relations, apply_to_list for general n-ary operators, or a suchthat construction with bound variables via Rewrite: apply bvar domainofapplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the appropriate elimination rule based on presence of bvar and operator class (relation vs general operator) so that domain restrictions become explicit in strict markup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewrite non-strict token elements (cn types and presentation MathML in tokens)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewrite cn elements with type attributes (e-notation, rational, complex-cartesian, complex-polar, constant) to strict cn via specific rules; rewrite any ci, csymbol, or cn containing presentation MathML into semantics elements (annotation) per rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalize numeric and token representations into strict cn/ci/csymbol forms; wrap tokens that contained presentation MathML in semantics/annotation-xml to preserve presentation information while producing strict content tokens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewrite operators to csymbol references
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewrite remaining operator elements defined in specific Content MathML sections to csymbol elements referencing the symbol identified in the syntax table; some operators require special-case symbol choices depending on argument types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be attentive to cases such as selector argument order, minus unary vs binary symbol choice, set operator choices depending on argument type, and statistical operator symbol choice depending on argument types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewrite non-strict attributes (type, definitionURL, encoding, other disallowed attributes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewrite remaining ci and csymbol elements with a type attribute to strict expressions with semantics (type annotation); where definitionURL and encoding can be interpreted as a content dictionary reference, rewrite to use the cd attribute; any elements with attributes not allowed in strict markup should be rewritten to a semantics construction with the element as first child and attributes in annotation elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert attribute-based, non-strict metadata into explicit semantics/annotation forms and prefer cd-based content-dictionary referencing over free-form definitionURL/encoding when possible.
